Job Type:
 
Permanent
 
About us 


K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate. 


We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.


About the role


In this role you will administer our employee electrical technical training programs as we seek to develop our national staff in a range of areas including mining, maintenance and processing. You will ensure that these programs meet K92 Mining standards and external training accreditation where necessary.


Key Accountabilities


Key accountabilities of this position include.




Develop and maintain training needs analysis, training plans, succession plans as well as the Apprenticeship and Cadet Traineeship programs


Administer the administration of the Electrical technical training programs including, Apprentice Program, Pre-Vocational Program, Technical Training Scholarships, In Plant Training and NATTB Trade Testing Program. 


Create Individual Development Plans (IDP) which document on and off the job training as well as work experience required to achieve career goals.


Liaise with statutory bodies and external stakeholders regarding professional membership as they impact with the registration’s procedures for fellow K92 member employees.


Provide progress reports and information in meetings and written reports on a weekly basis or as directed.


Do reviews and edit the Apprentice Program Policies, Technical Scholarships Program    to be in line with K92 `s business plans.


Assist to market the available training opportunities to employees and providing necessary information via training Calendars pamphlets and brochures.


Assist or relieve as required in all other professional areas of the HR section.


Evaluate and continuously improve training packages including trainer manuals and course materials.


Delivers work within approved budget managing any variances in accordance with escalation process.


Actively seeks cost reduction opportunities in all business relating to Training and Development.


Deliver training programs to K92 employees in accordance with training outcomes and agreed objectives including:


Personal Effectiveness Programs including delivering professional development programs as required by the business including, but not limited to, team skills (e.g., time management; dealing with change; managing conflict) and specialist skills (e.g., writing and presentation skills)


Leadership and Supervisory Development Programs including developing and delivering targeted leadership effectiveness programs such as performance planning, coaching for performance, safety leadership and time management for supervisors; and delivering K92 programs for the front-line manager and superintendents.


Actively promotes a safe and healthy culture.


Demonstrates personal responsibility for own health and safety whilst setting clear expectations of relevant legal obligations, safe workplace practices and HSE operating practices to others, holding them accountable for their actions.


Perform general housekeeping within and around responsible work area.


Conduct weekly meetings with the Coordinator Training and Development to review previous work and identify emerging issues and work.


Undertake required administrative tasks ensuring all documentation used in, and arising from, training and delivery and assessment is created, and maintained stored in accordance with K92`s accreditation and legal requirements.


Comply with K92`s quality and contractual requirements as well as relevant legislation.




About You 


To be considered for this role, it is essential that you




Possess Electrical training background with NEA certification


Certificate Stage IV in Training and Assessment


Sound practical skill in designing and reviewing competency-based training systems and experience with training packages.


Demonstrated ability to reinforce and develop training methods by being responsible for providing advice on and ensuring compliance with relevant legislation.


Sound computer literacy skills including operational efficiency in the Microsoft Suite, and industry-based programs such as PRONTO or similar programs.


PNG Drivers Licence -Class 6 essential


Level 3 Accreditation from National Apprentice Trade Testing Board (NATTB)


Experience in providing training and development advice to managers, superintendents, and supervisors preferably in metals extraction and mining operations.


Computer Proficiency in MS Office suite.


Well-developed interpersonal skills, particularly in presentations and facilitation.


An effective coach and mentor for industrial students, scholarship holders, apprentice, and graduates.


Self-motivated with ability to work under pressure and autonomously.


Strong active listening & interpersonal skills for rapport building, conflict resolution & training.




Life at K92  


K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.


Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.


At K92, we want all employees to share in our success, so as well as a competitive salary, employees also participate in our long- and short-term incentive plans, we also provide employees with access to savings incentive programs, medical assistance and the option to salary sacrifice for certain expenses.


In addition to all of this, employees can also access our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.

Position Title: Parts Logistics Officer


Location: Head Office – Port Moresby


Division: Boroko Motors


Overview


The Logistics Officer is responsible for coordinating with suppliers, shipping companies, freight forwarders, and transport providers to ensure the efficient tracking and delivery of sea freight shipments for the parts operations. This role involves monitoring shipment schedules, managing documentation, and ensuring timely delivery of parts to Boroko Motors’ branches and operations.


Key Responsibilities
- 
Coordinate with suppliers, shipping companies, and freight forwarders to arrange sea freight
   shipments.
- Track shipments from origin to destination, ensuring timely delivery and resolving delays.
- Review and manage shipping documentation including bills of lading, customs clearance and freight
  invoices. 
- Maintain shipment tracking reports and provide updates to management.
- Work closely with the procurement and parts teams to align shipment schedules with operational needs.
  
- Identify and resolve discrepancies in shipping documentation, delivery schedules, or freight charges.  
- Prepare and present logistics performance reports to management.
- Recommend improvements to logistics processes for efficiency and cost savings.
- Cross-train parts personnel to ensure shipment tracking and coordination can continue during absences.

- Experience in logistics, shipping coordination, or supply chain management.
- Strong attention to detail and accuracy in documentation.
- Excellent communication and negotiation skills with suppliers and freight partners.
- Ability to work under pressure in a deadline-driven environment.
- Strong organizational and analytical skills.
- Problem-solving ability to manage shipment delays or discrepancies.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office suite, particularly Excel.
- Knowledge of sea freight operations, customs clearance, and international shipping practices.
- Experience with automotive parts logistics would be beneficial.
- Familiarity with ERP or inventory management systems.
- Basic to intermediate computer literacy and the ability to learn unfamiliar systems quickly.
- High school diploma or equivalent, additional education or certification in supply chain or
  procurement  would be beneficial.
- Minimum five (5) years relevant experience in logistics, shipping coordination, or supply chain
  management, preferably in transport, automotive, or related industries.
- Proficient in logistics or inventory procurement software.

- Knowledge of automotive parts logistics and international shipping practices preferred

26344.description:
POSITION: Dean, Institute of Higher Education.


LOCATION: Popondetta, (Oro) Northern Province


DURATION: Three-year renewable contract with a 6-month probationary period


REMUNERATION: Competitive remuneration offered


ABOUT THE MODAWA INSTITUTE


The Modawa Institute is a newly established higher education provider in the Northern Province of PNG.  The Institute formally came into being as of 1 January 2024 but builds on more than 70 years of involvement in higher education within Papua New Guinea.  The Instutute is Registered with DHERST. There are three schools, each with a Head of School:




St Margaret’s School of Nursing and community health.


The Bishop Newton School of Theology.


The David Hand School of Teaching.




The institute seeks to develop a learning community where the various disciplines enrich each other, seeking to raise up leaders committed to excellence and innovation in their respective fields.


THE ROLE OF DEAN


The Dean will operate within the functions, roles and responsibilities outlined for the Principal in the Institute’s Canon (constitution) and under the guidance of the Chair of the Governing Council. 


The Dean will have oversight of the institution, leading a team of academic, administrative and support employees. He or she will be the Executive Officer of the Council, the team leader within the Institute and its public face in the wider community. The Dean will nurture the academic life of the Institute and teach within one of its schools. He or she will maintain academic currency, model scholarship within the institute and contribute more widely to academic discussion in his or her field. The Dean may initially also be a head of school for one of the schools of the Institute. 


He or she will have responsibility to oversight the administrative life of the institute, ensuring its financial and administrative integrity and ongoing viability. The Dean will be expected to encourage partners and build the financial base of the institute.


The Dean will be responsible for:




Maintaining and developing the ethos and vision of the college in line with Council strategies and directions.


Developing and leading a leadership team that will cultivate a positive environment for learning and work.


Collaborate closely with the other heads of schools.


Build the profile of the institute within the broader community and  strengthen relationships with business and industry representatives, donors, other Higher Education Institutions and national and overseas partners.


Contributing to the scholarly life of the institute.




KEY SELECTION CRITERIA


The Dean will hold, appropriate post-graduate academic qualifications in the relevant field.  He or she will have had significant experience in the higher education sector. The person will have experience in organisational administration, be fluent in written and spoken English, and have excellent presentation and public speaking skills. A commitment to uphold the ethos and values of the Modawa Institute is essential.


The Modawa Institute looks for staff who will are:




Deeply motivated by a care for young people.


Have a passion for learning.


Are self-starters and disciplined in their use of time.


Hold spiritual values in line with those of the Church.


Have a relationship style that evokes contributes to team building.




OTHER REQUIREMENTS


Under the Canon (constitution) of the Institute the Principal of the Institute (Dean) must be a communicant member of the Anglican Church of Papua New Guinea, or of a Church in Communion with the Anglican Church of Papua New Guinea.  If the Dean is also a Priest, he or she must hold a licence or permission to officiate from either the Archbishop or the Bishop of Popondetta.


CONDITIONS OF EMPLOYMENT


Remuneration:  By negotiation and in accord with qualifications and experience. A house on campus will be provided.  Relocation expenses by negotiation.


Applicants must have the right to work in PNG.


HOW TO APPLY:


Email your application to Modawa Institute with the following:




A cover letter addressing the following:




Your interest in becoming the Dean of the Institute.


Your educational leadership background and subject specialisations.


A description of your leadership style


Outline your teaching philosophy;




Your current resume;


A copy of your Academic Qualifications.


Two written references.




Email to: 
[email protected]
 





            

        
Apply

PNG MOTORS | PORT MORESBY


ACCOUNTS CLERK


Good with numbers? Even better with details?


We're looking for someone who knows their way around numbers, enjoys keeping things organised and understands that getting the figures right matters. Whether you've worked in accounts before or recently graduated with an accounting qualification, if you're someone who pays attention to the details, we'd like to talk to you.


As our Accounts Clerk, you'll play an important role in keeping the financial side of our business running smoothly. You'll be responsible for processing invoices, payments and financial transactions, maintaining accurate records, assisting with account reconciliations and supporting the finance team with day-to-day accounting activities. From checking figures to keeping paperwork in order, your work will help ensure everything adds up and nothing gets overlooked.


Previous experience in accounts or finance would be an advantage, but it's not essential. We also welcome applications from recent graduates with qualifications in accounting, finance or related fields. You'll need a good understanding of basic accounting principles, confidence using Microsoft Excel and a willingness to learn accounting systems. Strong numerical skills, attention to detail and the ability to manage competing priorities are important.


We're after someone who takes ownership of their work, communicates well and is willing to learn. Someone who understands that accuracy isn't just important in accounting. It's everything.


At PNG Motors, you'll be part of an established automotive business where teamwork, reliability and a willingness to get the job done are valued every day. Whether you're starting your career or bringing experience to the role, you'll have the opportunity to contribute to a busy finance team.

Goodman Fielder Papua New Guinea is one of PNG’s largest food companies, manufacturing and distributing high-quality Flour, Stock Feed, Snacks and Bakery products throughout the country. The company owns a host of iconic brands which include; Flame Flour, Flame Stockfeed, Bilas Bread, Arthur's Pie, Twisties, Skel Rice and the Meadow Lea range.


At GFI, we care about making everyday food better for everyone.


Our goal is to be the leading and most innovative food company with a mission to meet our customers’ needs for superior quality foods with brands that are trusted by families everywhere.  We are the go-to source of consumer, shopper, and customer insights to help our customer and business partners succeed.


We are seeking motivated and safety-conscious 
Process Technicians

29107.description:
Job Type:
 
Permanent
 
A
bout us 


K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate. 


We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.


About the role


Processing Services Operators are multi skilled technicians responsible for the day-to-day operation of the


•              mobile crushing and screening plant, conveying and stacking system.


•              concrete batching plant and agitator trucks


•              pastefill binder preparation plant


The Processing Services division operates on a continuous shift roster operating on both day and night shift.


Key / Major Accountabilities


Key accountabilities of this position include.




Perform the day-to-day operation of the mobile crushing and screening plant, conveying and stacking system; concrete batching plant and surface agitator trucks and pastefill binder preparation plant


Effectively operate and maintain mobile equipment including Light Vehicle, Front End Loader, Excavator, telehandler and forklift according to all K92 Operation & Maintenance procedures and fault reporting systems


Operate fixed plant equipment including jaw and cone crushers, screening plant, concrete batching plant, binder preparation plant, and cement offloading facility according to all K92 Operation & Maintenance procedures and fault reporting systems.


Monitor equipment and systems to ensure correct and safe operation.


Ensure quality of material being crushed, batched and prepared meets the correct quality standards by taking regular samples


Perform minor maintenance activities on all equipment and provide input and assistance maintenance personnel as needed.


Perform clean-up and housekeeping to ensure a safe, clean and productive work area.


Conduct machinery inspections throughout to ensure all systems are functioning properly.


Perform daily safety prestart maintenance checks.


Ensure all K92 safety standards, policies & procedures are always adhered to


Ensure that adequate duty of care is exercised in all aspects of work activities.


Ensure utmost compliance of Occupational Health and Safety Regulations and any site-specific rules which may apply within varying site operation.




About You 


To be considered for this role, you must have a Grade 10 Certificate or technical trade Loader and excavator licences and relevant experience as well as Valid PNG Class 3 and Class 6 licence. In addition to this you will have some or all the following.




Five (5) or more years relevant work experience


Experience with operation and maintenance of mobile crushing equipment including but not limited to jaw crushers, cone crushers, screens, conveyors and stackers


Experience with concrete batching plant operations.


High risk work certificates including, Working at Heights, Confined Space Entry, Equipment Isolation


Ability to perform duties with minimum supervision.


Ability to work shift work


Able to communicate effectively at all levels, with good written communication skills.


Self-motivated with the ability to work under pressure and autonomously.


Excellent attention to detail and time management skills.


Strong active listening & interpersonal skills for rapport building, conflict resolution & training.




Life at K92  


Our core values — Collaboration, Accountability, Respect, Excellence, and Safety — are central to our operations and fundamental to our success. K92 upholds a commitment to equal opportunity, striving to ensure that every individual can reach their highest potential without experiencing discrimination.


Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.


We believe in sharing our success with our employees. In addition to competitive salaries, we offer participation in long- and short-term incentive plans. We also offer savings programs, medical assistance, as well as access to our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster. 


If you share our values and are looking for your next career step, come join us on this exciting journey. Submit your application through our website today.

29051.description:
We at PNG Air pride ourselves as the leading domestic airline operating over 26 ports across the length and breadth of Papua New Guinea as the Airline of Choice. Operating the largest fleet of ATR 72-600 series in the region. We are committed to providing affordable world class experience with value fares and unbeatable cargo rates, ensuring reliable and safe on time service to our valued customers and stakeholders


Network Engineer


The IT Division is seeking to recruit a qualified 
Network Engineer
 
based in Port Moresby. This role is a Level 2 role which keeps PNG Air's LAN, WAN, wireless and security network available across Head Quarters, terminals and 30+ domestic stations. The role takes escalations from the Service Desk, resolves network incidents to root cause, and delivers network changes and new-site rollouts under change control.


Key responsibilities include the following:




Resolve L2 network incidents escalated from L1 (switching, routing, Wi-Fi,VPN,firewall, ISP links) within agreed SLAs; escalate to vendors or L3 where needed.


Manage, configure and maintain Sophos firewalls and switches, as well as routers andwireless controllers, including VLANs, routing, NAT, VPN and firewall/application-control policies.


Manage WAN connectivity across sites, including Starlink primary andDigicel / ISP secondary links, failover testing and ISP fault coordination.


Install, uninstall, relocate and maintain Starlink terminals, point-to-point and point-to-multipoint radios, RF links, antennas and other network equipment in Port Moresby, allPNG locations and overseas sites where applicable — including site surveys, mounting, alignment, cabling, power, testing, decommissioning and handover documentation.


Monitor network health in Zabbix; tune alerts, thresholds and dashboards and act onalarms before they become outages.


Raise and implement network changes through the Change Management process, withtested rollback plans.


Create RCA reports for network incidents, including all P1/P2 and recurring incidents,and track corrective actions to closure.


Deliver network builds for new sites, sales offices and airport stations using the NewSite LLD and IT Readiness Checklist.


Plan, install, terminate, test and certify end-to-end passive cabling (copper andfibre), including patch panels, racks, labelling and cable records.


Maintain network documentation: IP address register, topology diagrams,configuration backups and the asset register.


Manage network assets and inventories across all sites, including spares, serialnumbers, warranties, support contracts and lifecycle status, keeping records accurateand audit-ready.


Create SOPs, High-Level Designs (HLD), Low-Level Designs (LLD) and project reportsfor network work.


Apply firmware updates and security hardening in line with ISO/IEC 27001 controls.


Coach L1 and graduate team members through hands-on knowledge transfer.


Travel to outports and office locations as and when required for installations,decommissioning and on-site fault resolution; take part in the on-call roster.




Qualifications, Skills and Competencies:




Diploma or degree in IT, Computer Science, Electronics or a related field.


At least 6–8 years of hands-on, end-to-end enterprise network experience.


CCNA or equivalent required; CCNP, Fortinet/Sophos firewall or Aruba/Cisco wirelesscertifications preferred.


ITIL 4 Foundation preferred.


Experience in aviation, telecoms or a multi-site enterprise is an advantage.


Valid driver's licence and willingness to travel domestically.


Strong practical skills in the core tech

Late applications & applications submitted in hard copy will not be accepted.

System Administrator

System Administrator
 
based in Port Moresby. The role also runs Microsoft 365, Exchange and Active Directory, and keeps every certificate, licence and subscription renewed on time. Data centre and disaster recovery




Own the end-to-end operation of the primary data centre and DR site: servers, storage, power, UPS, cooling, environmental monitoringand physical access.


Maintain the DR plan, replication and failover runbooks; run DR tests at least twice a year and report RTO/RPO results.


Plan capacity, hardware refresh and lifecycle for compute and storage.




Virtualisation

Lead or support the migration off the current virtualisation platform with minimal downtime.




Backup and recovery




Run backup and restore across servers, databases, M365 and applications, including ransomware-safe offline and tape backups.


Verify backups daily and perform scheduled test restores.




Servers and operating systems




Administer Windows Server and Linux (Ubuntu) servers: builds, patching, hardening, performance and Docker-based workloads.


Manage file, print, DHCP, DNS and other core infrastructure services.




Database management




Administer SQL Server, PostgreSQL and MySQL: installation, upgrades, user access, backups, performance tuning and integrity checks.




Application management




Support business and enterprise applications (e.g. crew management, HRMS, finance, ITSM and in-house apps): installation, upgrades,integrations, access and vendor coordination.

Manage on-prem Exchange and support migration of remaining mailboxes to Exchange Online.


Administer Active Directory: users, groups, OUs, Group Policy, AD Connect sync, DNS and domain controller health.




Security, monitoring and change




Apply patches, hardening and vulnerability fixes in line with ISO/IEC 27001 controls; manage endpoint protection and privileged access.


Monitor servers, storage and applications in Zabbix and act on alerts before they become outages.


Resolve L2 incidents within SLA, create RCA reports for P1/P2 and recurring incidents, and raise changes through Change Managementwith tested rollback plans.




Documentation and team




Create SOPs, HLDs, LLDs, runbooks and project reports; keep server, application and asset inventories accurate and audit-ready.


Coach L1 and graduate team members through hands-on knowledge transfer; take part in the on-call roste

Operating from our Motukea headquarters and backed by established operations in Australia since 2015, we support major projects across Papua New Guinea and the Pacific.


We're a hands-on, solutions-focused business that values teamwork, innovation, and getting the job done right. While we take our work seriously, we also believe work should be rewarding, challenging, and enjoyable. We are committed to creating opportunities for our people to learn new skills, build successful careers, and be part of a supportive team environment.


 


2.  Role Overview


We are seeking a motivated and safety-conscious 
Junior Coating Technician
 to join our team. The successful candidates will assist with surface preparation, coating application, Inspection, and maintenance of equipment, steel structures, pipes, and other industrial components in accordance with company procedures, quality standards, and workplace health and safety requirements.


This is an excellent opportunity for an individual who is willing to learn, develop practical technical skills, and build a career in industrial coating and surface protection.

Assist with surface preparation, including cleaning, sanding, grinding, and abrasive blasting where trained and authorised.


Assist in applying protective coatings, paints, primers, and other coating materials.


Clean, maintain, and store coating tools, spray equipment, and other work materials.


Assist with checking surface cleanliness, coating thickness, and overall coating quality.


Follow work instructions, technical specifications, and coating procedures.


Maintain a clean, organised, and safe work area.


Wear the required personal protective equipment (PPE) at all times.


Follow workplace health and safety, environmental, and quality assurance procedures.




 


4.    Key Requirements




Grade 10 or Grade 12  with a technical or trade-related background.


A certificate or training in painting, coating, fabrication, or surface preparation is an advantage.


Willingness to undertake on-the-job training and obtain relevant competencies.






Required Skills for Role;






Strong willingness to learn and follow instructions.


Basic understanding of workplace health and safety.


Good attention to detail and commitment to quality workmanship.

29045.description:
Monier Limited the single largest producer, supplier and distributor or construction materials and building products in PNG is seeking to recruit suitably qualified and highly motivated individual for the following position:


HSEQ MANAGER


The HSEQ Systems Manager is responsible for the ongoing development and continuous improvement of Health & safety, environmentally sustainable and quality focused culture. This will be achieved through a systematic approach to planning and implementing of HSEQ Systems initiatives, setting clear accountabilities, consultation, communication, education/training and maintenance of Health & Safety, Quality and Environmental Management Systems.


This position is required to work closely with Executive and Senior Management, and operational personnel in the development, implementation, monitoring and review of Monier Limited’s Health & Safety Management System, Environmental Management System and Quality Management System.


Duties Include:




Undertake persistent examination and care to ensure that all resources and systems used by your division are adequate to comply with the duty of care required under the country’s Safety Act.


In consultation with key stakeholders, identify, plan and implement programs to achieve the strategic direction.


Provide advice and direction for all HSEQ matters.


In partnership with HSEQ Systems Supervisor/Coordinator, maintain records of all injuries and illnesses occurring at the workplace in accordance with legislative requirements and provide statistical summaries of these records as required.


Review, monitor and audit legal compliance by the ongoing development and review of the Company’s Health & Safety, Quality and Environmental Management Systems (policies and procedures). This includes ensuring the system meets accreditation requirements and Client pre-qualification status is maintained.


Identify and mitigate health, safety and environmental risks and potential incidents.


Provide HSEQ reports in accordance with internal management reporting requirements.


Ensure the implementation of Health and Safety consultative processes, including the Company’s Health and Safety Committee.


Maintain a thorough knowledge of current HSEQ legislation & requirements and ensure changes are facilitated through the business in a timely manner.


Work closely with the HSEQ Coordinators to ensure the provision of effective advice and support to the business.


Provide programs that ensure a safe workplace including safety orientations, skills training, emergency preparedness, proper instruction, hazardous material disposal procedures, use of protective equipment and promote a positive HSEQ focused culture.


Investigate and complete the process / close out of all Accident Investigation Reports and prepare/submit to management.


Assist Line Management, Supervisors and HSEQ System Coordinators in the effective application of subcontractor management to ensure safe work practices and compliance with Company’s policies and procedures.


Act as the Company representative at client meetings and industry forums.


Assist Business Managers to interpret HSEQ compliance requirements especially for license and permit obligations


Monitor compliance of projects and Company Business Units to quality, environment and safety procedures by ensuring regular inspection and audit is occurring.


Liaise with HSEQ systems users to identify and identified improvement opportunities.




Desirable Qualifications, Experience & Skills:




Tertiary Qualification in HSEQ or related disciplined.


Minimum of 5-10 years experience as in HSEQ at management role.


Experience in the implementation and development of procedures and programs.


Experience in maintaining systems in accordance with ISO14001, ISO9001, ISO45001 in a medium/key manufacturing organization.


Demonstrated commitment to maintaining a fit-for-work standard, including adherence to company alcohol and drug policies.


Reliable, punctual and willing to work overtime when required.


Willingness to share knowledge and provide coaching and mentoring to team members.


Flexible and adaptable, with the ability to work varied rosters and hours as required to meet operational and business objectives.


Strong organizational and multitasking skills, with the ability to plan, prioritize and complete work with minimal supervision.


A team-oriented individual with a strong work ethic and positive attitude.




Applications can be emailed to 
[email protected]
 or hand delivered to: Monier Limited office at Saraga Street 6 mile along with Cover letter, Updated CV with current passport size photo and names of 3 active referees. 


Applications should be addressed to:


Manager, Human Resources
Monier Limited,
P. O. Box 734, Port Moresby. NCD.


Applications close on COB Saturday, 07th November 2026. Position is POM based. Only shortlisted applicants will be contacted.





            

        
Apply

29030.description:
Assistant Warehouse Manager – Annex


BNG Trading Company Limited is the oldest and largest independent importer and distributor of food and consumer goods in Papua New Guinea. With a strong legacy and decades of experience, we have grown into a modern and dynamic enterprise, structured around three core business divisions. Our operations span the importation and distribution of a wide range of food and consumer products, commodity trading, and indent services.


 


We are seeking a motivated, experienced, and results-driven 
Assistant Warehouse Manager – Annex
 to support the Warehouse Manager in overseeing daily warehouse operations, inventory management, logistics, and distribution activities. This role is responsible for assisting in ensuring the efficient movement of goods, maintaining inventory accuracy, supervising warehouse teams, and upholding high standards of operational efficiency, safety, and productivity.


 


Key Responsibilities




Assist the Warehouse Manager in overseeing the daily operations of AX0 and AX1 warehouses.


Supervise and coordinate warehouse, inventory, invoicing, and administration teams to achieve daily operational targets.


Support the planning, coordination, and monitoring of warehousing, inventory, logistics, and distribution activities.


Ensure the efficient receiving, storage, picking, and dispatching of goods.


Maintain accurate inventory records and assist in conducting regular stock counts and reconciliations.


Monitor stock levels and coordinate with relevant departments to ensure timely replenishment and stock availability.


Assist in implementing warehouse procedures, inventory controls, and operational improvements.


Ensure warehouse equipment, forklifts, and vehicles are operated safely and report maintenance requirements.


Coordinate daily manpower allocation, staff attendance, and work schedules to meet operational demands.


Monitor warehouse productivity, identify operational issues, and recommend corrective actions.


Liaise with suppliers, transport providers, and internal departments to facilitate timely movement and delivery of goods.


Assist in preparing daily, weekly, and monthly warehouse operational and performance reports.


Support the Warehouse Manager in monitoring KPIs, coaching staff, and promoting teamwork, accountability, and continuous improvement.


Ensure compliance with workplace health and safety standards, company policies, and operational procedures.


Act on behalf of the Warehouse Manager when required to ensure continuity of warehouse operations.




 


Qualifications & Experience




Diploma or Degree in Management, Supply Chain, Logistics, Business Administration, or a related field.


Minimum 7 years' experience in warehouse operations, logistics, inventory control, or distribution, preferably with supervisory experience.


Sound knowledge of warehouse operations, inventory management, stock control, and distribution processes.


Experience supervising warehouse teams in a fast-paced operational environment.


Good computer literacy, including Microsoft Office applications and warehouse inventory systems.


Ability to prepare operational reports, analyse inventory data, and resolve day-to-day warehouse issues.


Experience in FMCG, wholesale, distribution, or similar industries will be highly regard

Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.


 


Join BNG Trading and contribute to the efficient management of warehouse, inventory, logistics, and distribution operations across our business.

28971.description:
Safety and Security Coordinator


 


Safety and Security Coordinator Position Description


 










Reports to:






Country Director






Work location:






Port Moresby










Department:






International Programs – PNG CO






Budget holder:






No










Grade






5






Direct reports:






No










 


Here you’ll make a difference


Save the Children is the world’s largest independent child rights development organisation, making a difference to children’s lives in more than 100 countries. From emergency relief to long-term development, Save the Children secures a child’s right to health, education, and protection. At Save the Children, we attract bright and big-hearted people who are inspired to make a difference. Together, we are fearless in our pursuit of making lasting change for the children and communities who need it most. In Papua New Guinea, Save the Children implements programs in the sectors of health, education, child protection, child rights governance, and livelihoods. 


 


Here your skills will be valued – Role Purpose


Reporting to the Country Director, the Safety and Security Coordinator (S&S Coordinator) is responsible for ensuring an effective safety and security management system that meets Save the Children’s minimum operating safety and security standards at all times in our operational areas. This will include the ongoing assessment of threats and risk to Save the Children programs and staff, and provision of advice to senior management to manage organization risk. As a member of the Senior Management Team, the S&S Coordinator supports the development of an organizational culture that reflects Save the Children’s mandate and values, promotes accountability and high performance, encourages a team culture of learning, creativity and innovation, and enables our people to deliver outstanding results for children.


 


Key Areas of Accountability


Safety and Security Compliance




Develop and ensure compliance with Save the Children’s safety and security operating standards and protocols. Monitor the security environment and adjust security policies and procedures accordingly.


Ensure that all staff are familiar with and adhere to the country-wide Safety and Security Management Plan (SSMP); ensure that the SSMP is up-to-date and refreshed at a minimum on an annual basis. 


Provide necessary support during emergencies, working closely with the Senior Management Team and Safety and Safety and Security Focal Points in the provinces. 


Support the Incident Management Team (IMT) in security-related crises. 


Ensure that safety and security strategies, frameworks, policies, and procedures are consistently applied across all Save the Children in PNG offices. 


Provide S&S planning, advice and guidance to Save the Children staff for field trips within the country.


Develop and provide regular security briefings/presentations to staff in English/Tok Pisin.




 


Risk Assessment and Analysis




Develop escalation triggers for security protocols and provide relevant information for decision-making. 


Ensure proper compilation and distribution of incident reports. 


Monitor security events and incidents, coordinating appropriate responses and follow-ups. 


Provide regular security updates, including situational analysis and recommendations, to the Country Director and Senior Management Team. 




 


Support Program Operations




Conduct security risk assessments for program areas/offices and recommend enhancements. 


Provide safety and security advice to field managers to support program operations. 


Provide technical support regarding the safe movement of staff, adequate safety and communications equipment in vehicles, and training of drivers in established procedures and requisite skills.




 


Communication and Training 




Liaise regularly with S&S focal points in the UN, NGO, government, and community leaders to gather and verify security information. 


Coordinate the flow of security information with relevant stakeholders and ensure its accuracy and reliability. 


Participate in formal or informal NGO security networks/forums and contribute to collective security analysis. 


Maintain and update incident reporting systems, ensuring timely dissemination of information to staff. Ensure that appropriate systems are in place to effectively disseminate security information and updates of the security system to staff


Oversee the use of S&S telecommunications systems (e.g., satellite phones) and alert the ICT Officer to any system failures. 


Conduct regular security meetings with relevant staff to review protocols and developments. Develop and implement a security training plan for staff, assessing their competency and ensuring their preparedness. 


Develop security briefing materials and provide orientation for incoming or newly appointed staff. Ensure security briefings are updated on a quarterly basis and conducted at each location within 24 hours of arrival.


Build capacity within the team for conducting threat assessments and security briefings. 




 


Child protection and safeguarding requirements




Maintain a child safe environment at the workplace and safeguard children’s rights, acting in the best interests of children at all times.


Maintain compliance with Save the Children’s 
Child Safeguarding Policy
, 
Code of Conduct
, and PSEAH policies and reporting processes among staff and volunteers.


Act as a role model by demonstrating highest standards of behaviour towards children in private and professional life.


Never abuse the position of trust that comes with being part of Save the Children’s family.


Maintain a safe and positive relationship when working with children and young people.


Respond to any concerns for the safety or wellbeing of a child in a program in accordance with internal reporting processes.




 


Health, safety, security and risk management 
 




Be a role model for safety and security and comply with all workplace safety policy, procedure, work instructions and training. Act safely at all times.


Report all incidents, injuries and potential hazards in a timely manner.


Participate in, and contribute to, health and safety awareness and improvements.


Be aware of, and consider, the risks associated with one’s daily work and apply appropriate mitigation measures in line with Save the Children’s policies and procedures.




 


All roles at Save the Children contribute to our impact for children.


At Save the Children, every role, whether in our programs or support services, plays a vital part in our impact for children. We are committed to creating a positive impact on the lives of children and their communities, and we value the contributions of every team member in achieving this vision.


 


Person Specification


It takes all types of people to do the challenging work we do. Here are some of the specific skills and experiences you’ll bring in this role:


 


Qualifications/Accreditations




Minimum bachelor’s degree in security and protective services, criminal justice, occupational health and safety, or a related field (or equivalent military/police academy diploma) – or a minimum of eight (8) years of comparable experience.


Minimum five (5) years of progressive experience in humanitarian or international development work – preferably in an NGO environment. 


Minimum three (3) years of security management experience in humanitarian, military, or law enforcement settings. 


Familiarity with Papua New Guinea’s security contexts, legislation, regulatory landscape, and emergency stakeholders.


Ability to implement and audit Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and safety compliance frameworks.


Competence in conducting risk assessments, threat analyses, and incident investigations.


Advanced knowledge of and experience with communication technologies. 


Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with fluency in English (both written and verbal) and Tok Pisin. 


Strong people management, training, and capability-building skills; ability to work effectively in a team.


Ability to work effectively under pressure in complex and challenging environments. 


Computer proficiency with a particular focus on MS Word, MS Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint.


Exhibit a strong work ethic with a high degree of flexibility with respect to working hours; ability to effectively plan and manage own time under pressure.


Proven ability to work in a self-directed and motivated fashion, with limited supervision.


Ability to think strategically, prioritise, and meet deadlines in a complex and challenging environment; must be culturally sensitive.




 


Additional Information 




Any offer of employment at Save the Children Australia will be subject to a satisfactory National Police Record Check and a Working with Children Check.


Employees must sign on to Save the Children Australia’s Child Safeguarding Policy and Code of Conduct.


Ongoing performance and employment will be measured against KPIs, values and demonstrated behaviours outlined above


Save the Children Australia is an Equal Opportunity Employer.












Save the Children is the world’s largest independent child rights development organisation, making a difference to children’s lives in more than 100 countries. From emergency relief to long-term development, Save the Children secures a child’s right to health, education, and protection. At Save the Children, we attract bright and big-hearted people who are inspired to make a difference. Together, we are fearless in our pursuit of making lasting change for the children and communities who need it most. In Papua New Guinea (PNG), Save the Children implements programs in the sectors of health, education, child protection, child rights governance, and livelihoods. Save the Children’s program portfolio includes Maternal Child Health programming, including most recently a project to improve maternal nutrition and maternal child health funded by DFAT in Simbu and East New Britain Provinces; and is therefore seeking a lead for this project.


 


Safety and Security Coordinator 


 


Reporting to the Country Director, the Safety and Security Coordinator (S&S Coordinator) is responsible for ensuring an effective safety and security management system that meets Save the Children’s minimum operating safety and security standards at all times in our operational areas. This will include the ongoing assessment of threats and risk to Save the Children programs and staff, and provision of advice to senior management to manage organization risk. As a member of the Senior Management Team, the S&S Coordinator supports the development of an organizational culture that reflects Save the Children’s mandate and values, promotes accountability and high performance, encourages a team culture of learning, creativity and innovation, and enables our people to deliver outstanding results for children.


 


Key Responsibilities 


Safety and Security Compliance




Develop and ensure compliance with Save the Children’s safety and security operating standards and protocols. Monitor the security environment and adjust security policies and procedures accordingly.


Ensure that all staff are familiar with and adhere to the country-wide Safety and Security Management Plan (SSMP); ensure that the SSMP is up-to-date and refreshed at a minimum on an annual basis. 






Provide necessary support during emergencies, working closely with the Senior Management Team and Safety and Safety and Security Focal Points in the provinces. 


Support the Incident Management Team (IMT) in security-related crises. 


Ensure that safety and security strategies, frameworks, policies, and procedures are consistently applied across all Save the Children in PNG offices. 


Provide S&S planning, advice and guidance to Save the Children staff for field trips within the country.


Develop and provide regular security briefings/presentations to staff in English/Tok Pisin.




 


Risk Assessment and Analysis




Develop escalation triggers for security protocols and provide relevant information for decision-making. 


Ensure proper compilation and distribution of incident reports. 


Monitor security events and incidents, coordinating appropriate responses and follow-ups. 


Provide regular security updates, including situational analysis and recommendations, to the Country Director and Senior Management Team. 




 


Support Program Operations




Conduct security risk assessments for program areas/offices and recommend enhancements. 


Provide safety and security advice to field managers to support program operations. 


Provide technical support regarding the safe movement of staff, adequate safety and communications equipment in vehicles, and training of drivers in established procedures and requisite skills.




 


Communication and Training 




Liaise regularly with S&S focal points in the UN, NGO, government, and community leaders to gather and verify security information. 


Coordinate the flow of security information with relevant stakeholders and ensure its accuracy and reliability. 


Participate in formal or informal NGO security networks/forums and contribute to collective security analysis. 


Maintain and update incident reporting systems, ensuring timely dissemination of information to staff. Ensure that appropriate systems are in place to effectively disseminate security information and updates of the security system to staff


Oversee the use of S&S telecommunications systems (e.g., satellite phones) and alert the ICT Officer to any system failures. 


Conduct regular security meetings with relevant staff to review protocols and developments. Develop and implement a security training plan for staff, assessing their competency and ensuring their preparedness. 


Develop security briefing materials and provide orientation for incoming or newly appointed staff. Ensure security briefings are updated on a quarterly basis and conducted at each location within 24 hours of arrival.


Build capacity within the team for conducting threat assessments and security briefings. 




 


Child protection and safeguarding requirements


--       Maintain a child safe environment at the workplace and safeguard children’s rights, acting in the best interests of children at all times. 


--       Maintain compliance with Save the Children’s 
Child Safeguarding Policy
,  
Code of Conduct
, and PSEAH policies and reporting processes among staff and volunteers.


--       Act as a role model by demonstrating highest standards of behaviour towards children in private and professional life.


--       Never abuse the position of trust that comes with being part of Save the Children’s family.


--       Maintain a safe and positive relationship when working with children and young people.  


--       Respond to any concerns for the safety or wellbeing of a child in a program in accordance with internal reporting processes.


 


Health, safety, security and risk management  




Be a role model for safety and security and comply with all workplace safety policy, procedure, work instructions and training. Act safely at all times.


Report all incidents, injuries and potential hazards in a timely manner.


Participate in, and contribute to, health and safety awareness and improvements.


Be aware of, and consider, the risks associated with one’s daily work and apply appropriate mitigation measures in line with Save the Children’s policies and procedures.




 


All roles at Save the Children contribute to our impact for children.


At Save the Children, every role, whether in our programs or support services, plays a vital part in our impact for children. We are committed to creating a positive impact on the lives of children and their communities, and we value the contributions of every team member in achieving this vision.


 


Person Specification


It takes all types of people to do the challenging work we do. Here are some of the specific skills and experiences you’ll bring in this role:


 


Qualifications/Accreditations




Minimum bachelor’s degree in security and protective services, criminal justice, occupational health and safety, or a related field (or equivalent military/police academy diploma) – or a minimum of eight (8) years of comparable experience.


Minimum five (5) years of progressive experience in humanitarian or international development work – preferably in an NGO environment. 


Minimum three (3) years of security management experience in humanitarian, military, or law enforcement settings. 


Familiarity with Papua New Guinea’s security contexts, legislation, regulatory landscape, and emergency stakeholders.


Ability to implement and audit Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and safety compliance frameworks.


Competence in conducting risk assessments, threat analyses, and incident investigations.


Advanced knowledge of and experience with communication technologies. 


Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with fluency in English (both written and verbal) and Tok Pisin. 


Strong people management, training, and capability-building skills; ability to work effectively in a team.


Ability to work effectively under pressure in complex and challenging environments. 


Computer proficiency with a particular focus on MS Word, MS Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint.


Exhibit a strong work ethic with a high degree of flexibility with respect to working hours; ability to effectively plan and manage own time under pressure.


Proven ability to work in a self-directed and motivated fashion, with limited supervision.


Ability to think strategically, prioritise, and meet deadlines in a complex and challenging environment; must be culturally sensitive.




 


Additional Information 


--       Any offer of employment at Save the Children Australia will be subject to a satisfactory National Police Record Check and a Working with Children Check.


--       Employees must sign on to Save the Children Australia’s Child Safeguarding Policy and Code of Conduct.


--       Ongoing performance and employment will be measured against KPIs, values and demonstrated behaviours outlined above


--       Save the Children Australia is an Equal Opportunity Employer.










How to Apply:


Your application should include a cover letter (2 pages maximum) together with a current CV and contact details of two recent referees, Certificates and current Police Clearance Certificate obtained in the last 12 months.


 


Interested Candidates are invited to submit their applications via email to:

please note applications will be accepted on a rolling basis, and the vacancy may close prior to the deadline. So, we encourage you to apply soon

28790.description:
Campus Administrator


 


The Modawa Institute is a newly established higher education provider in the Northern Province of PNG.  The Institute formally came into being as of 1 January 2024, but builds on more than 70 years of involvement in higher education within Papua New Guinea.  There are three schools, each with a Head of School:




St Margaret’s School of Nursing and community health.


The Bishop Newton School of Theology.


The David Hand School of Teaching.




The institute is seeking a suitably qualified and highly motivated general administrator, who will contribute to the development of this new higher education institute. Reporting to the Principal/ Dean, the Administrator shall oversee general (non-academic) administration of the campus. He or she shall be person with background in administration, preferably with experience in the education sector. Demonstrated financial expertise is advantageous.


Responsibilities




The Administrator shall work with the Dean and finance team on budget preparation, collaborate with accounts and finance staff, the accountant and auditor, to ensure accurate financial record-keeping, and ensure careful budgetary control.


He or she shall ensure compliance with labour laws, develop and implement human resources policies and procedures, performance evaluation, professional development as well as employee benefits and welfare programs.


The Administrator will work with the Principal/Dean to coordinate development and maintenance of institute grounds, buildings and other infrastructure in line with Governing Council planning and budgetary parameters.


He or she will work with the ICT officer to serve both academic and administrative functions.  


He will ensure that capital items such as vehicles, genset, mowers and are properly serviced and maintained.


He or she shall ensure efficient record-keeping, confidentiality, and compliance with data protection regulations and Governing Council policies. The Administrator will ensure compliance with legal and regulatory requirements, keeping up to date with relevant laws and regulations concerning education, employment, finance, and data protection.




He or she will directly supervise:




Finance staff


Drivers and ground staff.


Security officers.


Site officer


Maintenance workers (carpenters)




Term of contract
: Three years, with year one being probationary.


Appointment
: On nomination of the Dean, with confirmation by the Governing Council.


Accountability
: The Institute Campus Administrator shall report to the Dean.


Salary:  By negotiation and in accord with qualifications and experience.


Special requirements
:  The successful applicant must be willing to support the ethos and moral position of the Anglican Church of Papua New Guinea.


Applications
: Written applications, including a full curriculum vitae, nominated referees, and proof of educational attainments should be submitted by email to the Dean at: 
[email protected]

th

25532.description:
Job Type:
 
Permanent
 
About us 


K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate. 


We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.


 


About the role


This position will be responsible for administering the employee technical training programs to meet the business needs of the Exploration and Drilling departments at K92 mining limited.


To ensure that these programs meet K92 Mining standards and external training accreditation where possible and necessary.


 


Key Accountabilities


Key accountabilities of this position include.




Design, implement, and continuously improve training programs, including trainer manuals and course materials for the Exploration and Drilling Departments.


Develop Individual Development Plans (IDPs) and administer on-the-job and off-the-job training for Exploration and Drilling departments.

Division: Carpenter Shipping Agency


Location: 
Madang


Department: Administration


 


Overview


The Branch Manager is responsible for overseeing the overall operations, commercial performance, and administrative functions of the branch office. This includes managing vessel operations, customer service, sales, documentation, and ensuring compliance with company policies and international shipping regulations. The role demands strong leadership, strategic thinking, and in-depth knowledge of the shipping and logistics industry.


Key Responsibilities




Manage the day-to-day operations of the branch, including vessel handling, documentation, equipment control, and customer service.

Lead, train, and motivate a team to ensure high performance and operational efficiency.

Position Title: Contract & Service Manager


Location: Head Office – Port Moresby


Division: Daltron


 


Role Overview:


We are seeking a highly organized and customer-focused Contract and Service Manager to oversee the performance, delivery, and continuous improvement of Printer Services and IT Service Desk operations. This role is vital in ensuring service excellence, managing client contracts, driving SLA compliance, and aligning service management processes with business objectives in a system integration and managed services environment.


Key Responsibilities:


 Printer Services Management




Oversee all aspects of printer service operations, including maintenance, consumables, and device lifecycle management.


Monitor printer fleet performance and coordinate field support teams and vendors for timely issue resolution.


Ensure SLAs are met for uptime, service response, and consumable delivery.


Manage contracts related to MPS (Managed Print Services), hardware leasing, and OEM partnerships.




Service Desk Operations




Lead and manage the Service Desk team (Level 1 and Level 2), ensuring efficient logging, escalation, and resolution of incidents and service requests.


Ensure 24/7 or agreed operational support is in place with proper shift planning and resource allocation.


Monitor KPIs including FCR (First Call Resolution), SLA compliance, ticket volume, and customer satisfaction.


Implement and optimize ITSM tools and knowledge bases to support staff and end-users.




 Contract Management




Manage customer service contracts, including renewals, compliance, performance tracking, and reporting.


Review and negotiate terms with clients and vendors to ensure service alignment and cost-effectiveness.


Maintain accurate contract records and documentation in line with company standards and audit requirements.




 Service Management & Improvement




Implement and enforce ITIL-aligned service management processes (Incident, Problem, Change, Asset, and Configuration Management).


Analyze service performance and drive continuous improvement initiatives across all service lines.


Collaborate with Sales, Projects, and Technical teams to ensure smooth service transitions and onboarding of new customers.




 Reporting & Stakeholder Communication




Generate regular service performance reports for internal management and clients.


Conduct service review meetings and act as a primary point of contact for escalations.


Communicate proactively with stakeholders regarding service disruptions, planned maintenance, and changes.




 


Qualifications & Experience:




Bachelor’s degree in IT, Business Administration, or a related field.


Minimum 5+ years of experience in a service delivery or service desk management role, preferably within a managed services or system integrator environment.


Strong experience managing printer services (e.g., HP, Canon, Kyocera, Ricoh,Sharp) and IT Service Desk operations.


Proven understanding of contract management, SLAs, and vendor coordination.


ITIL Foundation certification (intermediate or expert level preferred).


Familiarity with ITSM tools such as SolarWinds, ServiceNow, Freshservice, or equivalent.


Strong leadership, negotiation, and customer engagement skills.

PMP, PRINCE2, or similar project management qualification.


Experience with KPI-driven environments and continuous improvement methodologies.


Knowledge of BPO/outsourcing models, especially in government or banking sector engagements.

Be part of a dynamic team delivering impactful ICT services across industries.


Work in a culture that values innovation, accountability, and customer satisfaction.


Opportunity to grow into senior leadership roles within a rapidly expanding services organization.

29028.description:
Newmont produces metals the world needs - safely, responsibly and with care for people, communities and the environment. With a 100+ year history, we continue to shape the future of mining through innovation and strong operational performance. By joining our inclusive, world-class team, you can help shape the future of mining and make a meaningful difference.


Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.


Purpose
Take the lead in our Gold Room operations as 
Supervisor Gold Room
, overseeing critical processing activities to deliver production targets while championing safety, efficiency, and continuous improvement across the operation.


Essential Duties




Lead daily Gold Room operations, ensuring safe, efficient, and reliable production outcomes.


Drive operational performance by monitoring processes, identifying opportunities for improvement, and optimising workflow efficiency.


Champion compliance with standard operating procedures (SOPs) to maintain operational discipline and consistency.


Foster a strong safety culture by ensuring adherence to security requirements, safety standards, and company policies.


Conduct routine safety inspections and risk assessments, proactively identifying and mitigating potential hazards.


Troubleshoot operational challenges and implement practical solutions to minimise downtime and maximise productivity.


Analyse process performance data to identify trends, improve efficiencies, and support continuous improvement initiatives.


Maintain accurate and timely records relating to production, maintenance, and safety performance.


Take ownership of risk management activities, ensuring risks are identified, controlled, and continuously monitored.


Collaborate closely with maintenance teams by raising and tracking plant defect notifications to support equipment reliability and operational excellence.




Training & Experience




Qualification in Process Plant Operations or Metallurgy or equivalent


Previous experience in a Gold Room, metallurgical processing, mineral processing, or gold extraction environment.


Demonstrated leadership or supervisory experience within a processing plant or operational mining environment.


Strong understanding of Gold Room operations, gold recovery processes, and associated equipment.
Proven ability to lead teams safely while driving operational performance and achieving production targets.


Experience monitoring plant performance and analysing process data to identify improvement opportunities.


Demonstrated problem-solving skills with the ability to troubleshoot operational issues and minimise production disruptions.


Knowledge of maintenance management processes, including raising work requests and identifying plant defects.


Strong record-keeping, reporting, and administrative skills with a high level of attention to detail.


Excellent communication and stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to work effectively across operations, maintenance, and technical teams.


Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications and mine site operational systems.


Current driver's licence.




Working Conditions
This is a FIFO role on a 21/21 roster.

29026.description:
Newmont produces metals the world needs - safely, responsibly and with care for people, communities and the environment. With a 100+ year history, we continue to shape the future of mining through innovation and strong operational performance. By joining our inclusive, world-class team, you can help shape the future of mining and make a meaningful difference.


Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.


Purpose
You'll be responsible for executing complex lifts that enable mining, maintenance, and infrastructure projects to be completed safely and on schedule. Your expertise, commitment to safety, and precision will help drive operational success while ensuring the highest standards of performance across site.


Essential Duties




Conduct Prestart Checks – Conduct comprehensive inspections of the crane that has been allocated for operation. Documenting crane maintenance status and reporting any faults or non-compliances.


Plan and Risk Assess – Conduct site inspections prior to set up of the crane commences in which they will assess the site for hazards and determine the most suitable crane and approach for the lift.


Preparation and Set Up – Set up the crane correctly at all times according to WHS legislation, site policies and procedures and manufacturer’s instructions.


Operation – Operate the crane in accordance with WHS legislation, site policies and procedures and manufacturer’s instructions. Interpret load charts correctly to calculate safe working loads ensuring that all lifts are within the crane’s capacity. Monitor the rigging of loads and commence lifting only when safe to do so.


Critical / Non-Standard Lifting – Understand the complexities of critical and non-standard lifting activities and comply with both site and industry standards while performing the lifts.


Pack Up / Post Operational Checks – Strict adherence to WHS legislation and Newmont policies and procedures. Pack up and post operational checks performed as per the manufacture’s instruction.


Reporting of any operational issues, faults or defects via supervision and documenting in the maintenance logbook.


Team leadership – Act in a leadership capacity and make crucial decisions that maintain the safety of the surrounding work area.


Ensure that all controls are always in place when the work area specific to their crane is operational.




Training & Experience




Prior relevant work experience essential in fixed plant maintenance and heavy industry.


Must be familiar with and understand safe work procedures that are relevant to the operation of mobile lifting equipment.


Proficient in English with excellent verbal and written communication skills.


Sound, analytical, and critical thinking skills. Ability to solve problems in often high-pressure situations.


Excellent communication skills.


Strong active listening & people skills.




Working Conditions
This is a FIFO role on a 28/14 day and night rotational roster.
